root_cause.text: The sleepable buildid file reader in lib/buildid incorrectly accessed file contents through direct page-cache folio loading with read_cache_folio()/filemap paths instead of the standard __kernel_read() interface, exposing an unsafe faulting path that could dereference NULL in filemap_read_folio.
root_cause.evidence: The fix removes the sleepable-context logic from freader_get_folio() that did `read_cache_folio(...)` when `r->may_fault` was set, and replaces it in `freader_fetch()` with `__kernel_read(r->file, r->buf, sz, &file_off)`, while the CVE/commit message explicitly says this change is to “Prevent a ‘BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference in filemap_read_folio’” and that `__kernel_read()` “handles all the complexity of reading file data.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the missing `linux/fs.h` header so filesystem-related symbols are available and the file builds correctly.
intent_record.what: A single include directive was added to the file: `#include <linux/fs.h>` immediately after the existing `#include <linux/pagemap.h>` line.
intent_record.how: This makes filesystem-related declarations, types, and macros from `linux/fs.h` available to this compilation unit, allowing references to those symbols to compile correctly and resolving missing dependency issues at build time without directly changing runtime logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Restrict freader_get_folio() to page-cache-only lookups by removing on-demand folio reads and failing immediately when the folio is not already cached and uptodate.
intent_record.what: The change removes the explicit secretmem_mapping() rejection and deletes the conditional fallback path that, when may_fault was true and the folio lookup failed or returned a non-uptodate folio, took the invalidate lock and called read_cache_folio(); the function now only performs filemap_get_folio() and then errors out if the result is invalid or not uptodate.
intent_record.how: At runtime, freader_get_folio() no longer faults in or reads missing page-cache folios from storage and instead succeeds only when the target folio is already present and uptodate in page cache. This prevents blocking/page-fault-style cache population in this path and causes uncached or stale folios to fail immediately. The removed secretmem check no longer returns a dedicated early error, but such mappings will also fail unless a usable uptodate folio is already obtainable through the cache lookup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Handle secretmem files safely and use __kernel_read() in sleepable contexts to avoid invalid folio-based access.
intent_record.what: The change inserts two new conditional paths in freader_fetch() before the existing folio-based fetch logic: one checks secretmem_mapping(r->file->f_mapping) and, if true, sets r->err to -EFAULT and returns NULL; the other checks r->may_fault and, if true, reads sz bytes into r->buf using __kernel_read(r->file, r->buf, sz, &file_off), returning the buffer on exact-size success or setting r->err to either the negative read error or -EIO and returning NULL on short/failed reads.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents the function from attempting to access secretmem-backed file mappings, which are intentionally inaccessible, and adds an alternate read path for sleepable contexts so data can be fetched with __kernel_read() instead of the existing folio/pagemap mechanism. This avoids invalid access for secret memory and enables safe reading when page faults or sleeping are allowed.

relevance_review.reason: This change only adds a missing filesystem header for build correctness. It does not alter the buildid file-reading logic, replace page-cache folio access with __kernel_read(), or address the unsafe faulting path behind the NULL dereference.

The group directly changes the sleepable file-reading path to use __kernel_read() instead of folio/page-cache based access, and adds safe handling for secretmem files. This matches the root cause of unsafe direct folio loading in lib/buildid leading to NULL dereference in filemap_read_folio.

The change directly modifies the unsafe folio-based file reading path in lib/buildid by removing on-demand page-cache reads and only allowing cached, uptodate folios, which is a direct mitigation of the vulnerable read_cache_folio/filemap access path described in the root cause.

candidates.rationale: This is the direct page-cache folio read path identified in the root cause. In sleepable contexts it performs on-demand folio loading instead of using __kernel_read(), exposing the unsafe filemap_read_folio path.

This call is the sleepable buildid reader entry into the vulnerable folio-based access path. It directly triggers the unsafe freader_get_folio logic rather than using the safer __kernel_read() interface.
This condition explicitly enables the faulting/sleepable path that attempts to populate folios on demand, which is the behavior the fix removes in favor of __kernel_read().

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement performs direct page-cache folio loading for the sleepable buildid reader, invoking the unsafe on-demand filemap/read_folio path identified in the root cause instead of using the safe __kernel_read() interface.
This statement is the call site that routes sleepable buildid reads into the vulnerable folio-based access path, thereby triggering the unsafe direct page-cache loading behavior.
This condition gates the sleepable faulting path and enables on-demand folio population when the folio is missing or not uptodate, which is the unsafe behavior removed by the fix.

Author: Andrii Nakryiko <andrii@kernel.org>

    lib/buildid: implement sleepable build_id_parse() API
    
    Extend freader with a flag specifying whether it's OK to cause page
    fault to fetch file data that is not already physically present in
    memory. With this, it's now easy to wait for data if the caller is
    running in sleepable (faultable) context.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the exact newly introduced sleepable file-reading path inside `freader_get_folio()` and how `build_id_parse()` enables it via `may_fault=true`. The vulnerable construct is present: when `r->may_fault` is true, the code does direct page-cache folio loading using `read_cache_folio()` instead of using `__kernel_read()`. Specifically: `r->folio = filemap_get_folio(r->file->f_mapping, file_off >> PAGE_SHIFT);` and then `if (r->may_fault && (IS_ERR(r->folio) || !folio_test_uptodate(r->folio))) { ... r->folio = read_cache_folio(r->file->f_mapping, file_off >> PAGE_SHIFT, NULL, r->file); ... }`. The root cause says the vulnerability is that the sleepable buildid reader accesses file contents through direct page-cache folio loading with `read_cache_folio()/filemap` paths rather than the standard `__kernel_read()` interface, exposing an unsafe faulting path. This commit introduces exactly that behavior for the sleepable API: `build_id_parse()` now calls `__build_id_parse(..., true /* may_fault */)`, and `freader_init_from_file()` stores `struct file *file` plus `bool may_fault`, enabling the unsafe path. There is no sign of the fix here because the code still uses `read_cache_folio()`/`filemap_get_folio()` and does not switch the sleepable reader to `__kernel_read()` or any equivalent safe kernel read interface. Therefore this commit version contains the bug and does not yet contain the fix.
